question.worked_solution:
To find the rank of $D,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 6 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $3$ non-zero rows).

Therefore, $\text{rank}(D)=3.$
